“And that was a mistake, wasn’t it!?” Margaret snapped. “If we’d known how he’d drag you down-”

“Margaret,” Phillip interrupted, placing a hand on her arm. “We discussed this. We said we’d wait.”

“Drag me down?” Danny repeated. “Drag me down!?”

“I know,” Margaret said to her husband, ignoring Danny. “But I just… I can’t anymore.” She turned to her oldest son and said, “Daniel, we know.”

“Know what?”

“What you did in El Paso,” Phillip said.

There was a beat of silence, Danny’s expression slowly turning from anger and confusion to something that looked like worry, before it was wiped blank. Buck had straightened up in his chair and he, too, seemed worried as he looked between Danny and their parents.

“About…” Phillip looked uncomfortable and glanced to his wife. “Your side-jobs.”

Buck drew in a sharp breath.

“What side-jobs?” Dannny asked, voice as blank as his face.

“The prostitution, Daniel!” Margaret wailed.

“What?” Eddie was not the only one who said it, Maddie’s and Chimney’s voice joining his. Eddie turned to Buck, to see his reaction, but his boyfriend’s worried gaze was fixed entirely on Danny. There was no surprise on Buck’s face, Eddie realized. None of the shock and horror that Eddie was feeling, that he was seeing on Maddie. Just concern.

“Wh- What?” Danny’s voice cracked.

“If we’d known,” Phillip said, “we would’ve helped you. You didn’t have to- to sell yourself like that. You could’ve come home.”

“Who… Who told you about…”

“Your friend was worried about you,” Margaret said. “That nice detective.”

“Detective?” Danny’s voice was quiet and shaking, the color draining from his face.

“Yes, Lucas Drake, he said-”

Eddie didn’t get to hear what Lucas Drake, whoever the hell he was, said. Before Phillip was even done talking, Danny was running. Buck got to his feet, his chair toppling to the floor, but he didn’t even get his brother’s name out before the apartment door was thrown open and Danny was gone.

Chapter End Notes

Someone way back on Chapter 20 of Against the Current commented, wondering if Daniel's cancer being back was going to be the secret in my version of 4x04/05. And obviously it wasn't, but I had to bite my tongue so hard not to point out the OTHER things that could come out.

Chapter 32

Chapter Notes

CW for frank conversations involving harassment by authority figures, sex work, sexual coercion, rape, and similar topics.

See the end of the chapter for more notes

Buck paced on the sidewalk, phone pressed to his ear. It rang and it rang, before going to voicemail. Again. Just like it had every other time that he’d tried. Which just made everything even more stressful, because Danny always answered when Buck called. The only time he hadn’t, Buck came home to find him sitting in the dark and spiralling over - as Buck later found out - a possible cancer diagnosis.

When Danny ran out of the apartment, Buck had not been far behind. He’d been right on his brother’s heels until his brother got into his car and tore out of the parking lot, heedless of Buck calling after him. Buck had been left standing on the sidewalk, watching him drive away and at an utter loss for what to do.

“Any luck?” Eddie asked. He had come down when Buck didn’t go back upstairs. Maddie, too. They’d both stood there watching him pace, the unspoken question in their eyes.

“No,” Buck said. He huffed, just barely caught himself from kicking the building in a fit of pique, and tried a different tact.

This time, it rang only for a couple moments before the other end picked up.

“What?” Albert asked through what sounded like a full mouth.

“Is Danny there?”

“Isn’t he with you?”

Buck let out a frustrated breath and hung up, before he bit Albert’s head off. He got his answer, anyway: Danny was not at their apartment, either. And with how he’d been driving, he probably would have made it there by now if that was where he was headed.

There was one other place he could be.

“He’s here,” was how Austin answered the phone.

“Oh thank God,” Buck breathed, feeling himself relax.

“He won’t tell me what happened, though.”

“Um. Mom and Dad, they found out about, uh.” Buck glanced at Maddie and Eddie. “Something that he used to do in El Paso. Besides firefighting.”

“The hookering.”

“Of course you know about it.” He honestly wasn’t even surprised by it, because of course Austin knew.

“How did they find out?”

“Some guy named Drake-”

“Oh,” Austin said, and then the call dropped. Buck was left staring at his phone, feeling like he’d missed something major.

“So?” Maddie pressed.

“He’s at Austin’s,” he said, putting his phone away. “Mom and Dad?”

“Chimney’s handling them,” Eddie said. “You weren’t surprised. You knew.”

There’s the question he’d been waiting for. Except it wasn’t a question, just a statement of fact. Because Eddie knew him better than almost anyone, maybe as well as Danny. Maybe better than Danny, in some ways.

“Yeah,” Buck breathed out.

“This entire time?”

“Not the entire time.”

“When did you find out? How did you find out?” Maddie asked, rubbing at her pregnant stomach. When Buck just shrugged, unwilling to answer, she scowled but moved on to, “So who’s Detective Drake?”

“Fuck if I know,” Buck blurted out. “Danny doesn’t like cops, hasn’t since before we left Hershey. Athena’s the only exception, and I have no idea how that even happened.”

“Something about her abusing her authority for revenge against May’s bullies.” 

Yeah, that tracked. Danny would most definitely appreciate something like that in someone else. Though, Buck wondered when and how his brother heard about that. It had to have been pretty early, because after they found Abby’s mom, he remembered Athena mentioning that she and Danny had exchanged numbers. Buck hadn’t spent any time at all dwelling on the oddness of it, simply accepted it without any question.

(Mom always did call him self-centered.)

Maddie started to head inside, back to Chimney and their parents. She paused just inside the doorway to the building, however, to turn to Buck and say,

“I’m sorry.”

Not knowing how to respond, Buck simply nodded. Maddie grimaced in return, but continued on inside all the same. Neither Eddie nor Buck were in any rush to follow her, neither of them very interested in spending any more time with the Buckley parents.

“I looked up to him,” Eddie suddenly said, breaking the silence.

Buck felt his hackles raise as he spun around to face his boyfriend. He opened his mouth to ask what, exactly, the other man meant by that, but then Eddie was shaking his head and speaking again.

“I didn’t- I didn’t mean it like that,” he hurriedly said, hands warding away any angry words Buck might’ve spewed. “I just meant, he used to make it look so easy. It was just the two of you, and somehow he seemed to have it all together, you know? He never looked like he was struggling. I was working three jobs before I moved up here, trying to make ends meet for me and Chris. Even afterwards, with the department salary, it was still a struggle, and I kept thinking, “Danny wouldn’t be struggling like this.” He just always made it look so easy.”

“We didn’t have any furniture when we first moved to El Paso,” Buck admitted. “Nothing except what we took from our bedrooms at home. Then one day after school he took me to pick out a couch and then a table, then all this other stuff. Showed up with practically the entire store for Christmas. I always just thought it was the pay from the fire academy, but…”

But the stipend while going through the fire academy didn’t pay that well, Buck knew. The same was true for the salary of a first year firefighter. He’d been a stupid teenager who simply accepted what he was being given, and then never thought about it as he got older. He just took it for granted that his big brother could turn lead into gold.

(He really had been self-centered, hadn’t he?)

“I’ve never seen Danny look like that before,” Eddie said. “The way he looked when your mother mentioned a detective. He looked like you did, when…”

When Buck overheard Eddie and Shannon, was the end to that unfinished thought. When Buck decided to run and kept running.

Buck had never seen his big brother so- so- Afraid wasn’t the right word for it. To call it fear was close to what it was, but it didn’t fit quite right with what was on Danny’s face before he fled. Perhaps dread was a better descriptor.

Neither Buck nor Eddie lingered for much longer, both of them deciding against going back upstairs and dealing with whatever was happening between Maddie and the older Buckleys. Buck felt a moderate amount of guilt for abandoning his sister to them, but she had Chimney with her. The guy needed to start getting used to keeping her company at ground zero of their family drama, because it would inevitably become a regular thing if Maddie still insisted on their parents being around more.

Buck spent the night at the apartment, in case Danny came home, and he found himself unable to sleep very much out of worry. But Danny never walked through the door, leaving Buck tired and wired when their shift rolled around. Worse, when he got to the station, he found that the c-shift driver-engineer - Richard Stoppard, who replaced Dixon when the man retired a year and a half ago - was pulling a double. Because Danny had called in.

This, obviously, just made Buck even more concerned. Because while Danny was perfectly willing to miss a shift of work if Buck needed him, he very rarely called in for his own sake. Buck remembered having to practically wrestle him back into bed as a teenager, when Danny was suffering from the flu and still insisted on going in.

But on this day, Danny had called in. Unprompted, as far as Buck was aware. It was an act that might as well have been accompanied by a giant neon sign saying “SOMETHING IS WRONG.” Austin also didn’t show up for his shift, according to Edddie. That, somehow, made Buck worry less in one way and a lot more in another. Because Danny had been with Austin. Because if Austin thought he had to skip work to stay with Danny, then something was seriously wrong.

There was a point in the shift, in the early afternoon, where Buck was thankful that Danny hadn’t come in. He was just cleaning up in the kitchen when Flowers came to tell him that he had visitors. His gut was already squirming by the time he got to the truck bay, because somehow he knew exactly who had shown up.

His parents looked entirely out of place, standing awkwardly just inside. They were looking around the place with interest, smiling politely at the others as they went by with their tasks. Buck, for a moment, thought about turning around and just ignoring them. But his footsteps echoed across the bay and his parents snapped their attention to him, and it was far too late to run away now. Not without them causing an even bigger scene about it.

“Mom, Dad.” He tried to keep his tone upbeat and friendly, he really did. But it had been years since he’d had to deal with them on his own, without the promise of Danny swooping in to shield him, and he was dreading whatever this conversation was going to be. “I didn’t expect to see you here.”

“Daniel’s ignoring our calls,” Dad said. “Your mother and I thought we’d come see him in person. We knew his station number, but he never got around to giving us an address for either of you.”

Thank God for that. Danny was probably trying to avoid a repeat of Junior year, where their parents just showed up at their door while he was at work.

“Danny’s not here,” Buck told them, ignoring his mother’s frown at the nickname. “He called in.”

“Is he okay?” Mom asked, sounding genuinely concerned. She looked genuinely concerned, too. There was a different flavor to it than the concern she always showed Buck growing up.

“I don’t know. I haven’t heard from him since he left last night.”

“Running away and hiding isn’t like him,” Dad said.

“We’d expect that kind of behavior from you,” Mom said, and her frown turned sharp. “We never should have let him leave with you. You always were such a burden, never thinking about anyone but yourself. If we had known how you were going to ruin him-”

“Margaret,” Dad interrupted, placing a calming hand on her arm. Buck's feet felt glued to the floor, and his face was burning. “Maybe this isn’t the time or place?”

“He can’t run away from-”

“Hey, Buck!” Jon Mendoza called. His voice was strained, and the polite smile he wore was a knife’s edge. The expressions on Flowers’ and Nola’s faces, just behind him, were not kind. “I think Cap was looking for you.”

It was a lie, Buck realized immediately. It was also an out and he took it with both hands, giving them a grateful nod as he ran past. He didn’t go all the way into the station proper, instead taking a quick left into the locker room and throwing himself onto a bench as far from the door as possible. Once more, he was extremely grateful that the 133’s locker room had actual walls and not the glass of the 118’s.

He was hiding away, he knew that he was. But he wasn’t going to risk going back out there and finding his parents still lurking. It was already humiliating enough that his coworkers got a front row seat to his mother’s familiar scolding, he had no intention of giving them more of a show. So he stayed there, tucked away in the corner of the locker room with his legs drawn up, until the alarm rang.

Mom and Dad were gone when Buck ran for the trucks. And while he could tell the others wanted to ask something, say something, none of them did, for which he was more than a little grateful.

By the time his shift had ended, he’d gotten nothing from Danny. He’d gotten a couple texts from Austin after badgering him, mostly consisting of variations of him telling Buck that his brother was “fine.” Which did absolutely nothing to assuage the anxiety that had lodged itself in Buck’s stomach since his brother’s flight.

Suffice it to say, he’d hurried out of the station and maybe broke a couple traffic laws on the way to the apartment. Danny wasn’t there, which meant he was still at Austin’s. Which meant that Buck just dumped his bag in the living room and turned to head out.

Buck opened the door to find Maddie standing there, fist raised to knock.

“Danny’s not here,” he said.

“Oh.” Even with the mask on, Buck could see his sister’s expression drop.

“I was about to head to Austin’s,” he told her. “C’mon.”

She nodded, waited for him to lock the door, and then followed him back down. She tailed him in her own car for the short journey to Austin’s building, and then he had to impatiently wait for her to catch up after he practically sprinted for the entrance when he was done parking. They took the elevator up, even while Buck wanted to just run up the stairs.

He probably would have gotten there faster.

Buck led the way to the right door, with the shiny 5C hanging on it. He knocked, and then knocked again, until a resigned looking Austin opened the door. The man had a towel slung over his shoulder and was wearing an old concert tee for the Smiths. He stared at the two of them for a moment, and then just stepped to the side with a sigh and a,

“Dan!”

Danny appeared from the other room and since Buck could see a bed through the open door, he assumed it was the bedroom. His brother was wearing clothes that were not his, a pair of sweatpants with what looked like a tomato sauce stain on the knee and a sweatshirt with a ratty hole near the hem. Maddie made a questioning sound, but Buck ignored it as he hurried to Danny.

“You weren’t answering your phone,” he said, and winced at the way it sounded accusatory.

“Yeah, sorry, I…” Danny trailed off with a sigh and rubbed at his face. “Why are you two here?”

“You ran away and ignored us,” Maddie said. “Why do you think we’re here?”

“Do we have to do this now?”

Danny sounded tired, and small, and more than a little pathetic. Buck immediately hated himself for barging in here, even though being able to lay eyes on his big brother did more to ease his worries than any text from Austin could possibly have done. But he was still worried, and terrified, because something was wrong, and Danny wasn’t telling him. Again.

“You promised,” was what Buck said. “Remember?”

Then he immediately felt awful for it when Danny groaned, shoulders falling with more than just exhaustion. Still, he made his way to the couch and threw himself down onto it. Austin drifted to stand just behind him, and Buck had the impression of a sentinel standing guard.

“Seriously?” Danny asked, incredulously, when Buck - instead of taking a seat on the couch or the chair - perched on the coffee table in front of him. Buck felt sheepish for a moment, and then just shrugged. “Whatever. Just… Say or ask or whatever it is you’re here for.”

Buck saw Maddie, having taken her mask off, open her mouth. But he spoke up before she could say anything, knowing that her questions would probably be about their brother’s side jobs and not the most pressing matter at hand.

“Who’s Drake?” he asked.

“A bastard,” was the answer, apparently, but it wasn’t Danny who said it. Austin did, the usual stoic expression marred by clear anger.

“Mom and Dad said he was your friend,” Maddie said, and the response to that was a sharp and bitter laugh from Danny.

“Yeah, no,” he said, shaking his head. “Listen, I’m alive, you’ve seen me. Can we just-”

“Danny,” Buck interrupted. “Please.”

Danny sighed and dropped his head with a groan.

“He was the cop who arrested me,” he said, one hand rubbing at his wrist. The motion caught Buck’s attention, had him frowning as his mind nagged at him.

“Arrested you for what?” Maddie asked, but they ignored her.

“In El Paso?” Buck’s thoughts were whirling. “That was- That was years ago. Why did he wait until now to tell Mom and Dad about… Y’know, that?”

“Because I told him no again,” was his brother’s quiet answer. Danny wasn’t looking at him, eyes fixed on his lap.

“Because you…” Buck looked at his brother’s wrists once more, and he remembered the marks that had been on them before they went to Texas. He remembered his brother’s quip - the deflection - about his sex life. He reached out, gently gripped at his brother’s wrist, and lifted it up. “Danny?”

Danny refused to meet his eye, giving a little shrug. Maddie’s expression was slowly morphing from confusion to horror. But Austin just gave a single slow nod when Buck turned to him.

“Danny,” he repeated, anguished. “How long- Has it been this entire time?”

“Not the entire time,” his brother finally answered. “I thought- He was in El Paso. And now he’s here.”

“Dan, why?” Maddie sounded appalled. “You tried to convince me to leave Doug. You called the cops on him. Why would you…?”

“He threatened Buck,” Danny said, and his voice broke with the words. “Threatened to have CPS take him away. And then he threatened Chris.”

Buck tasted bile as he surged to his feet.

He had to- He had to- He had to do something. He was supposed to make Danny better, right? That was his job, just like Mom kept telling him. She almost definitely didn’t have this in mind, but-

He had to do something.

“Get your shoes on,” he croaked.

“What?” Danny asked, finally lifting his head to look at him.

“Get your shoes on,” Buck repeated. And then, “Please, Danny.”

Danny stared at him for one long moment. Then, to Buck’s relief, he let out a sigh and he got up.

Daniel saw the house they were pulling up to and fixed his baby brother with a glare.

“Seriously?” he spat.

“She can help,” Buck said, although he sounded more hopeful than certain. He turned to Maddie in the front passenger seat. no doubt for her support in this… Whatever this was. “Right?”

“Right,” their sister agreed, more firm than Buck’s wavering confidence. “Of course she can.”

“I’m sure,” Daniel grumbled and looked back out the window to glare at the Grant residence. He could see Athena’s car in the drive, along with another that must’ve been May’s, and Nash’s truck. Which was just wonderful.

They trooped up to the door, Daniel dragging his feet. It was Buck who knocked, glancing over his shoulder as he did like he was checking to make sure that Daniel hadn’t done a runner. Which was fair, Daniel supposed. Running was what Buckleys did, and he’d proven that he wasn’t the exception to that rule. Though, Austin would probably stop him from getting too far. He was too approving of this idea, and hadn’t even asked before coming along.

When Nash - because of course it was him - answered the door, his face flickered from surprise, to something close to elation, and then confusion.

“Hey, Buck.” Nash smiled at Daniel’s brother, and then peered past to the rest of them. “I was expecting Michael at the door. Not that this isn’t nice.”

“Hi, Bobby.” Buck gave an awkward wave. “Uh, we- Well, Danny needs to talk to Athena about something.”

Daniel would much prefer to not talk about this, thanks very much. Not that he was being given much of a choice in this matter. There was an irony to this whole thing, but if he pointed it out, his baby brother would probably cry.

(Why couldn’t he be allowed to just hide under a blanket at Austin’s for another day or two?)

“Sure, come on in,” Nash said, a curious frown on his face.

The first thing Daniel noticed when they got downstairs was that the firepit had been replaced since May’s graduation party, and in its spot was a fireplace almost identical to the one that Michael and Nash destroyed. The second thing that he noticed was that there were an awful lot of balloons in the kitchen-slash-dining room. Along with what might have been the leftover plasticware from the aforementioned graduation party.

“Oh, no, were you guys celebrating something?” Daniel said, trying to aim for remorse and landing flat. “And we’re interrupting. We should-”

Austin, in the ultimate act of betrayal, grabbed his arm before he could even start to head for the front door. Daniel glowered at him, not that it seemed to bother the other man any.

“Dan needs to talk to you,” Austin told Athena.

“Traitor,” Daniel hissed, tugging his arm loose.

He watched Athena’s eyes flicker to the door of May’s room, at the top of the stairs. Then she nodded and said,

“We’re waiting for Michael to get here with the cupcakes. Let’s go sit outside.”

“I’ll, um. I’m gonna call Carla,” Buck said, holding his phone up. “She might know what to do about any bogus CPS calls.”

It was a statement that had the sergeant lifting one elegant eyebrow. It had Daniel scowling - at his brother, at himself. It also had Daniel feeling a little bit thankful that at least he wasn’t going to be made to talk about this in front of his baby brother. 

With a smooth jerk of her head, Athena led them out onto the back patio. Maddie settled herself into a chair, relief at being off her feet evident on her face, with Daniel throwing himself into the one next to it. Athena sat down across from them, and none of them spoke at first.

“Well,” she said, glancing at Nash who came to sit beside her after closing the sliding door. “What did you want to talk to me about?”

“Dan,” Austin urged when Daniel didn’t speak up. He was standing just at his shoulder.

Daniel just glowered at the glass of the patio table.

“Fine,” Maddie huffed. “At dinner, Mom and Dad said… They brought up something Dan apparently used to do in El Paso. They said some detective named Drake told them.”

“Lucas Drake?” Athena asked, an edge to the way she said the name.

Daniel gave a snort.

“Made his acquaintance?” he asked, a twist to his lips that might’ve passed for a smile in the dark.

“I never asked where in Texas he was from,” the sergeant stated. “Didn’t particularly want to know more about him.”

“Good choice.”

“How do you know him?”

Daniel shrugged but did not answer. Above him, he heard Austin sigh in annoyance. A small, bratty part of him took joy in that fact.

“He’s blackmailing Dan,” Austin said. Daniel lifted his head to scowl up at him.

Neither Athena nor Nash said anything right away, the sergeant frowning at Daniel with a furrowed brow.

“With what?” she finally asked.

“Dan,” Austin prodded, when he was once again reticent about speaking up

“He said this Drake person threatened Buck, and now Chris,” Maddie answered for him. “Mom and Dad mentioned- They said-” Daniel heard his sister’s voice tremble. He looked away from her and across the Grants’ backyard. “Prostitution, Daniel?”

Daniel found that, even if he wanted to speak up, he had nothing to say to his sister. She sounded as upset as Buck, when he found out about it.

“Well.” Nash sounded awkward, and Daniel had to force himself to keep from grinding his teeth at the sound of the man’s voice. “There’s… There’s nothing to be ashamed about-”

“Ashamed?” Daniel snarled at him. “Ashamed!? I was able to put food on the table, keep a roof over his head, get him what he needed when he needed it. I was able to get him birthday gifts and Christmas presents and new clothes and school supplies. I was able to make sure my kid was taken care of! Why the fuck would I be ashamed of that, you sanctimonious piece of-!?”

“Danny?” Buck’s worried voice cut through the rising volume of Daniel’s own. His brother was half-out of the now open sliding door, phone pressed to his shoulder. Michael and Harry had shown up at some point and were at the dining table, having stopped in the middle of setting out cupcakes onto a tray to gawk. “Is everything okay?”

No.

“Everything’s fine, squirt,” Daniel grumbled, sitting back down. He hadn’t even realized he’d gotten to his feet. His brother, rudely, did not immediately take his word for it, instead looking to Austin.

“Okay…” Buck said, hesitant but clearly trusting whatever he saw from Austin. Daniel could’ve sworn he saw his baby brother glaring at everyone else, an angry Golden Retriever, before he slipped back inside and closed the sliding door once more.

“How- How did it even start , Dan?” Maddie asked, distressed.

“Needed the money,” Daniel said with a careless shrug. “Those first few months in El Paso weren’t exactly a cake walk, Mads.”

“But you could’ve-”

“Could’ve what? Gone to you and Doug for help?” He spat out the man’s name and watched his sister flinch. “Or maybe I could’ve taken Evan back to Mom and Dad? You’ve seen how they treat him. You heard the way Mom talks to him. He was happy in El Paso, Maddie. Happy to be away from them. Anything was worth keeping that. I promised to take care of him, and I did.”

“When did Drake come into it?” Athena broke in. Her voice sounded different, somehow, and Daniel wondered if he should start mentally calling her Sergeant Grant now.

“I got arrested,” was the simple answer.

He remembered being in that cramped, poorly lit interrogation room. He remembered being handcuffed and terrified, certain that he’d finally fucked up beyond recovering. And then Lucas Drake walked in, all swagger and the stench of cigarettes that never seemed to go away. Daniel’s instincts screamed that he couldn’t trust a cop, that he especially couldn’t trust this cop.

But Drake smiled as he loomed right over Daniel, bracketing him with his arms, telling him that surely it was all just a misunderstanding and promising that he’d get it cleared away. Daniel was too relieved at the time to look the gift horse in the mouth.

“I guess he thought I was pretty,” Daniel quipped. “Or he just liked the desperation.”

None of them seemed to appreciate his humor.

“And then he started threatening Buck,” Athena stated. It wasn’t a question.

“Yup.” When she stared at him expectantly, he sighed and added, “First responders are mandatory reporters, y’know.”

“That’s what Buck meant by bogus CPS calls,” Nash said, more a thought spoken aloud.

“Yup.”

Not that that had been the only threat.

(“What do you think they’d do to him, if he had to spend a night in jail?” Drake would whisper into his ear. “What do you think would happen to him if I ever got tired of you?”)

“Then Buck left El Paso, and I left El Paso,” Daniel said. “And it didn’t matter anymore.”

“Until Drake transferred here,” Athena said. “And started threatening Chris.”

“But it was… It was pointed out to me that Eddie isn’t me,” he said. “He’s an idiot, but he’s a good dad. They wouldn’t just take the kid.”

“What was Drake blackmailing you for?” Nash, bless him, asked.

Daniel bared his teeth at the man and replied with,

“What does anyone want from a whore?”

He took pleasure in the way Nash cringed and recoiled. He did not take pleasure in the way that, when he glanced over at the muffled cry his sister let out, he saw Maddie’s face twisted into anguished horror. Athena’s reaction was different, no horror or disgust: her nostrils flared in what was probably fury; her fingers dug into the tabletop in such a way that, if she had claws, he’d worry about her scratching the glass.

“Look, I love my brother,” Daniel said, before she could get righteous about anything. “But I’m pretty sure I sheltered him too well.”

“What do you mean?” Maddie asked.

“I mean, what’s the point of this?” he asked in return. “Nothing’s going to happen, not to Drake.”

“Dan…”

“Am I wrong? Hey, Sergeant, whatever happened to that cop who pointed a gun at Harry?” Daniel asked, and became the target of Athena’s glare. “Besides absolutely nothing.”

“There was an investigation,” she said, seething with every word. “Maynard pushed for disciplinary action.”

“And? Was there any? Anything more than a stern finger wag?” When she didn’t answer, Daniel scoffed and shook his head. “Cops investigating cops for being cops. My word against his. A whore’s word against his.”

“Stop calling yourself that!” Maddie snapped.

“Would you prefer prostitute? Hooker? Escort?”

“Courtesan,” Austin broke his silence to suggest. Daniel tilted his head back to smile at him.

“That makes me sound fancier than I am.”

“You said you were very pretty arm candy.”

“I was,” Daniel agreed, and then sighed as he turned his attention back to the other three. “Nothing’s gonna happen to him. You know it, I know it, we all know it. We had sex, it was…”

“Rape?” Athena’s voice was quiet and sharp. 

Daniel flinched. He wasn’t the only one.

“I was gonna go with “awful,” but that works, too. Good luck proving that, though,” he told her. “It’ll be fine, it’s not the first time I had to put up with Drake being upset that I told him no.”

“And how did the last time go?” Nash asked, far too snidely in Daniel’s opinion.

“It went,” he snapped back, and didn’t mention that it hadn’t stopped until he moved to Los Angeles. He got the impression that they’d already guessed that much, anyway.

“He went to your parents?” Athena wasn’t even directing the question to Daniel, instead focusing on Maddie. He huffed in irritation, an act which went ignored.

“Yes,” Maddie answered. “And then Mom ambushed Dan at dinner.”

“Probably what he wanted, or close to,” the sergeant growled. “I’ll get an EPO sorted out, until we can get a restraining order in place.”

“Did you not-” Daniel started to say, but Athena cut him off rather ruthlessly.

“Him going to your parents like that is harassment. And you very much implied he’ll do, and keep doing, similar things in the future. That I can prove.” She got up and straightened her blouse, glancing at her son and her ex-husband through the glass of the sliding door. “May managed a big call the other day, and we’re celebrating. It’s a surprise for her. You’re all welcome to stay for it, we have cupcakes.”

She stalked inside, and Maddie was not too far behind after she pushed herself out of her chair. This left Daniel and Austin outside with Nash, which was not a good thing. Especially when the fire captain opened his mouth.

“What I was going to say earlier is that there’s nothing to be ashamed about doing what you need to do for- for your kids,” Nash said. “I understand-”

“I don’t need your pity or your understanding,” Daniel bit out. And then, because he couldn’t help himself, “I managed to raise my kid to-”

A hand clapped over his mouth. Daniel immediately jerked his head back, a bit frantic, and scowled up at Austin, who dropped his hand and winced apologetically at him. Nash didn’t try to say anything more, he simply got up and stomped into the house.

Austin sat down in the chair that Maddie had vacated. Daniel glanced at him and scoffed and said,

“Shut up.”

Austin, predictably, continued to not say anything. And he sat out there with Daniel until Daniel was ready to go inside.

Chapter 33

Chapter Notes

CW continuing on from last chapter - talk of sex work, sexual exploitation, Det. Drake being an awful creep, abuse of authority, references to past domestic abuse.
(also, in case it's not obvious - part of this chapter takes place concurrently with part of last chapter.)

Eddie was not entirely certain what to think about everything - about what little - he’d learned last night. What he’d learned about Danny, and the fact that his boyfriend had known for however long and hadn’t said a damn thing. Not that he could blame Buck for keeping quiet about it, he did have siblings of his own, after all. But still, he and Buck told each other just about everything. That a small part of him was hurt by there being a secret was inevitable, even if Eddie was doing his best to ruthlessly crush it.

He had always looked up to Danny, that wasn’t a lie. From the moment he held Chris in his arms for the very first time he knew that it was Buck’s older brother whose example he wanted to follow. Hell, before that even: part of why he’d enlisted was because he knew that Danny would go to any lengths he needed to take care of Buck.

Apparently Eddie had not been wrong with that assumption, either.

After his discharge, after Shannon left him and Chris, when he was trying to juggle three jobs and was still falling short, it had been Danny’s example Eddie was striving for then, too. What he was constantly comparing himself to. Because Danny had made it look so easy, so effortless. Eddie could not understand why he wasn’t managing to do the same for Christopher, why he was still struggling even after he joined the Los Angeles Fire Department. 

The answer was that apparently he hadn’t truly considered, hadn’t truly known, which lengths that Danny would go. The answer was that they both chose to sell their bodies, if through different ways and by different means. And Eddie did not know what to think, what to feel, about that.

He did know, however, that he was entirely unnerved by Danny’s reaction. Considering he’d developed the same view of Danny that Buck had, and he knew he’d stuck the man on a pedestal, seeing him look so horror stricken and then watching him run from everything was disturbing.

When Eddie walked into the station the morning after the second disastrous dinner with the Buckley parents, two things became apparent: Austin was not coming in, as the driver-engineer for B-shift was loudly complaining about having to pull a double; and Chimney seemed just as bewildered as Eddie felt. The paramedic kept shooting him not-so-subtle glances from the moment he spotted Eddie, clearly dying to talk about everything.

Chimney hounded Eddie’s steps as he headed for the loft stairs, responding to Buck’s anxiety-ridden texts about Danny not showing up for work while he went. Eddie remembered the rants from Buck that he suffered through during high school, about Danny’s stubborn ass not calling in even though he was brain-meltingly sick, so he understood why Buck was getting worked up about it. Hopefully the knowledge that Austin was also out, and presumably with Danny, would help calm Buck’s nerves at least a little.

On the brightside, getting to watch as Chimney edged closer and closer to, maybe literally, bursting at the seams was kinda hilarious. Eddie took his time getting himself coffee, deliberately stretching out every step, while Chimney hovered around him, getting increasingly more and more red faced. The moment he clearly reached his limit and opened his mouth, Eddie beat him to it with the question of,

“How were Margaret and Phillip afterwards?”

It visibly threw Chimney off, leaving him flustered for a moment.

“They were… God.” The paramedic heaved out a sigh as Eddie poured a tad bit too much creamer into his coffee. Or not enough, depending on one’s personal views. “I don’t even know. Things were just so awkward after you guys chased after Dan, and then Maddie got into it with them when she came back up.”

Eddie didn’t suppose he had to ask what that had been about. Or maybe he did, since there were so many possibilities. 

“Did they say anything else?” he asked, taking a sip of his coffee and letting out a hum of appreciation.

“Nothing important.” Chimney’s tone was dark. When Eddie glanced at him curiously, he looked around before saying, “They were talking to each other while I cleared off the table. Mostly about Buck and Dan. Like I said, it wasn’t important.”

“I can probably guess the kinds of things they were saying about Buck,” Eddie told him, taking his coffee with him as he went for one of the couches. Chimney sat himself in one of the chairs, perched right on the edge and vibrating out of his skin. Eddie eyed him. “It’s killing you, isn’t it?”

“Did you know!?” Chimney finally burst out. “About-”

“No,” Eddie said, cutting him off. “I was as surprised as you.”

“Did Buck?”

Eddie just shrugged. Chimney scowled, very clearly not satisfied with the lack of an answer.

“So there was a deep, dark Buckley family secret,” the paramedic stated, sitting back in the chair. 

“I don’t think it counts when it’s only two people out of the entire family.”

“Then Buck did know!”

Eddie let out a sigh and debated the possibility of drowning himself in a cup of coffee.

“Buck knew what?” Hen asked as she joined them. Chimney immediately sat up in the chair, back ramrod straight and eyes wide. “Okay, what’s his deal?”

“Dinner last night was a disaster,” Eddie said, before they had to witness Chimney combusting. “They make me realize how lucky I’ve been with mine.”

“Aren’t your parents still pretty much ignoring your existence?”

“Like I said.”

The shift felt longer than usual, with Eddie having to deal with Buck’s anxiety-filled texts - which got worse after the Buckleys apparently made a surprise visit to the station - and the B-shift driver-engineer filling in for Austin, Eric Carver, complaining about having to come in. Apparently, he’d had plans for the day. Even though Eddie didn’t know the man very well, despite how long Eddie had worked with him and his whatever relationship with Danny, he figured it was a safe bet that Austin would not feel an ounce of guilt.

There was also Chimney, who really did look on the verge of exploding if he didn’t talk to someone about Danny. And since Eddie knew about it, too, it meant he found himself the unwilling participant of conversations that just went ‘round and ‘round. At one point, though, he volunteered to help inventory the ambulance and just about dragged Hen inside with him, slamming the doors shut.

When their shift ended, when Eddie was ferrying Hen back to her house so he could pick up Chris, he was not surprised when she turned slightly in her seat and simply said,

“So. Dan.”

“I hope he isn’t telling everyone.”

“Chimney and I tell each other all the new gossip, just like you and Buck,” she said. When he gave her a pointed look, she rolled her eyes and added, “And just like me and Karen. You’re dating your best friend, Eddie, of course I’m gonna compare some of what the two of you do to me and my best friend.”

“Firstly, I’m pretty sure Chris took my spot as Buck’s best friend-”

“Yeah, yeah, whatever, cry about it later,” she interrupted. “But, Dan.”

“Chimney better not keep spreading it around.”

“He won’t.” Hen sounded confident about that, so Eddie decided to trust her. He was definitely gonna mention it to Buck, though. Or maybe warn Maddie directly, let her handle that. “You had no idea at all?”

“Not a clue,” he said. “I kinda feel like I’ve been cheated.”

He could feel Hen’s gaze on him.

“What do you mean?”

“I mean that I was always envious of how easy he made it look. Being a single parent,” Eddie clarified. “I was working three jobs before I moved up here, and I was struggling even after Buck introduced me to Carla. I always thought Danny managed to do it because he was Danny. But it turns out that he was-”

He cut himself off with a huff. Eddie wasn’t sure he could even say it. It felt wrong to say it.

“When do you think Buck found out?” Hen asked.

“I have no idea.”

Chris was already set up at the Wilsons’ dining table and in the middle of class when they got there. So Eddie hung around with Hen and Karen, and with little Nia. It helped distract him from the way that there was a concerning amount of silence from Buck, after the single text saying he was going to Austin’s after his shift.

Eddie didn’t hear from Buck until after they got home, Chris heading for his room while Eddie stood in the kitchen and debated if he should figure out something to cook for dinner or just order something. Last time, it had been Albert who’d delivered, which had been simultaneously hilarious and awkward. They’d ended up giving him an even bigger tip than they usually would, because Eddie knew he wouldn’t be able to look him in the eye otherwise.

He’d just decided on pizza, and was digging out the menu for Bryce’s Slices when he heard the front door open and close.

“In here!” he called out, and a minute later Buck was joining him, throwing himself into one of the chairs at the table. Eddie could not help but think that his boyfriend looked awful. “Chimney told Hen about the, y’know.”

“I’ll mention it to Maddie. She can, I dunno. Yell at him for it, make sure it’s only Hen.”

Eddie nodded.

“How’s Danny?” he asked.

“He’s…” Buck let out a sigh, dropped his face into his hands and groaned. “He’s with Austin, right now. But I dragged him over to talk to Athena.”

“Because of the… Thing?”

Buck lifted his head to stare flatly at him.

“No, not because my big brother used to prostitute himself.” His tone was desert dry as he spoke. “Or, not… Not entirely because of it. I also called Carla while they were talking, to- Crap, I should’ve called Hen, too. She’d know how to handle a CPS visit.”

Eddie felt his heart stop.

“Why would you need to know that?” he demanded.

“Because you might get one.”

“Why?”

“That detective, Drake, he’s been blackmailing Danny,” Buck said. “He’s been threatening Chris.”

“Wh- What? Threatening to do what? For what?”

“The same thing he threatened me with, apparently,” he said. “To call CPS and have them take me away.”

“But why?”

“For…” Buck grimaced. “Please don’t make me say it, Eds. I don’t want to say it.”

For a moment, Eddie did not understand. For a moment, his brain refused to understand. But it came crashing into him regardless of any refusal.

“He was having sex with Drake?” Eddie asked, the words acidic on his tongue. “To- To keep me from losing Chris?”

Buck gave one small nod. Horror filled Eddie, from the tips of his toes to the top of his head, and he had to rush for the trash can. It felt like he retched up everything he’d eaten that day, and perhaps everything he’d eaten the day before. His stomach was twisting like a wet towel, trying to expunge everything. He was left gasping for air by the time he was done, and was grateful for the glass that Buck shoved at him.

“I’m sorry,” Buck whispered, and if Eddie wasn’t too busy drinking water he would’ve asked just what the hell he was talking about. His expression seemed to say it for him, however, because his boyfriend continued with, “I think this is all my fault.”

“You- What?” Eddie sputtered. “How is this your fault?”

“I didn’t even notice, just took everything for granted. Mom always called me selfish and self-centered. They both stopped by the station yesterday so she could call me a burden. And she wasn’t wrong, was she? I’m supposed to make him better. But instead… If it wasn’t for me, Danny never would’ve started- And Drake never would’ve-”

Buck let out a sigh and dragged a hand down his face. Eddie stood there and stared at him, the glass of water clutched in his hand. He was speechless for a moment, unsure what to say. Except, as he realized, he knew exactly what to say, didn’t he?

“You do what you have to for your kid. You be their dad, and you find a way to make it work. It doesn’t make them a burden,” Eddie said. He could tell from the twist of Buck’s face that he wasn’t making headway, or enough headway. “Is it Chris’ fault that I got shot?”

“What!?” Buck just about shrieked. “No! Of course not-”

“Then how is what happened to Danny your fault?”

Buck opened his mouth, closed it, opened it again, and then closed it once more. He huffed and his jaw took on the mulish set that made him look even more like Danny. Buck was self-centered, Eddie could admit that, it just wasn’t in the way that bitch Margaret meant. It was in the way that had Buck looking at this whole mess and somehow blaming himself for it.

“You were getting pizza?” Buck said, finger tapping the menu flyer for Bryce’s Slices that Eddie had dropped on the table.

“Yeah.” He accepted the subject change readily enough. He was relieved for it, really. “Figured we won’t risk Albert showing up at our door that way. Are you sticking around? Spending the night?”

“Danny said he might go back to the apartment tonight,” Buck told him. “I don’t want to leave him alone. But yeah, I’ll stick around for dinner with you guys.”

“Alright. Go ask Chris what he wants on his pizza.”

“Like he’ll say anything different from the usual,” Buck joked, already leaving the kitchen. “I want garlic knots!”

“Yeah, yeah.”

Daniel was getting increasingly close to the end of his tether, and he could feel his temper fraying like edges of the hole in the borrowed sweater he was still wearing. He loved his sister, he loved his brother, he just… He just wanted them both to stop and leave him alone. Luckily, Buck had left for Eddie’s shortly after dropping everyone back off at Austin’s apartment building.

Unluckily, Maddie had not followed their brother’s lead.

“I’m fine!” Daniel snapped for what felt like the fiftieth time as he slammed the cabinet door closed. “What happened to the Skittles that were in here?”

“You ate them,” was the answer from Austin. Daniel huffed and threw his hands up in exasperation.

“Yeah, you’re sure acting fine,” Maddie scoffed. She’d claimed an arm chair for herself, presumably because her feet started bothering her as much as she was bothering Daniel. “We need to talk about this, Dan.”

“I already did, you were sitting right next to me.”

“Dan-”

“Fine, whatever!” Daniel snapped. “But does it have to be right here? Right now?”

“If not here, where? If not now, when? Because we both know that you’ll just keep running away from it.”

“Like you?”

“Yeah, like me,” Maddie agreed, so easily that Daniel was taken aback. “You prostituted yourself, Dan! You-”

She suddenly stopped and turned to glare at Austin, who was idly dusting off the shelves that his little figurines were on. He was currently running a rag around the red dragon that Daniel had gifted him two Christmases ago, which somehow ended up front and center of the whole display. After the silence lasted for a beat too long, though, and he turned to see Maddie staring at him, Austin let out a quizzical,

“What?”

“Is that what this is?” Maddie demanded, lumbering to her feet. “Dan said that it’s not real, that it’s fake. Are you…?”

“What the fuck , Maddie?” Daniel spat.

“She’s not wrong,” Austin said, going back to the dusting.

“What!?” Maddie was visibly seething. “Listen here, you-”

“He’s not interested in sex,” Daniel nearly yelled. “Not with me, not with anybody. I’ve told you what this is. None of it has changed just because you found out I used to charge by the hour. I’m not some pitiful damsel getting victimized by the handsome firefighter. You don’t have to save me, not from him.”

“You think I’m handsome?”

“Shut up, Austin.”

“Well excuse me for worrying,” Maddie snapped out. “Why didn’t you tell me?”

“Oh, yeah, because you’re taking it so well now.” Daniel rolled his eyes.

“No, not about that!” she shot back. “Not just that. Why didn’t you tell me about Drake? Why did you hide it from me?”

“Why didn’t you tell me about Doug?” 

“That’s different,” she argued, voice quiet. “That’s… It was different.”

“Yeah, you’re right,” Daniel snarled. “I never went around telling everyone that he loved me while covered in bruises.”

Maddie’s expression went tight. Austin, having moved onto the bookcase behind her, froze and then drooped where he stood with a sigh. Daniel felt his stomach drop at the same time that his sister grabbed her purse and stomped for the door, tearing it open and slamming it behind her.

“Fuck,” Daniel whispered, tugging at his hair.

“I’ll make sure she gets to her car okay,” Austin said, dropping the rag onto a table.

“Thanks.”

Daniel flopped face down onto the couch, ignoring the other man’s amused snort as he went out the door, too. He stayed that way until Austin returned and even afterwards, listening to him putter about. It was nice, even as he stewed in the knowledge that he should not have said what he said to his sister.

“I should apologize to her,” he said, mostly into the black-grey-white-purple striped pillow. “Shouldn’t I?”

“I’m not your mother,” Austin remarked. “Or your therapist. But at least you’re feeling bad about this one, you little psycho.”

“Nash deserved it, Maddie didn’t.” Daniel pushed himself up. “Why did I say that?”

“I just told you I’m not your therapist, ask her.” He paused in the act of cleaning to fix Daniel with a stare. “You probably should talk to her, anyway. Does she know Drake’s bothering you again?”

Daniel didn’t bother answering, which was an answer in itself.

He stuck around for a bit longer, reluctant to head back to the apartment where he would no doubt be subjected to his baby brother’s hovering. Honestly, he’d prefer to spend another night with Austin, but neither one of them could afford to skip another shift of work and Daniel didn’t have his uniform here. So he eventually dragged himself out and to his car, taking the short journey to his own place.

After he parked, Daniel hesitated to get out. It was well into the evening now, and there were plenty of spaces to hide between his car and the entrance to the building. He knew how this went, knew how Drake worked. He’d gone through this before.

This time, he didn’t even make it more than two steps away from his car before being accosted by cigarette smoke and a Texan drawl.

“How’s Mommy and Daddy?” Drake asked, stepping out from behind a truck.

Daniel froze on instinct, which was absolutely the wrong thing to do. It gave Drake the opportunity to cross the space between them. Hurriedly moving back was also the wrong choice, as his back was soon hitting metal.

“They’re fine,” Daniel bit out. “Happy I’ve made friends.”

“Aw, are you upset with me?” Drake smirked, took a drag of his cigarette, and then blew the smoke directly into Daniel’s face. “I thought your parents would be proud of their little whore. You’re so good at it, after all. Y’know, except for how you’ve been ignoring me!”

The change in tone and volume was sharp, and it had Daniel cringing back as much as possible.

“I was trying to be nice,” Drake said, though there was nothing nice about his smile. “Remind you of your place, let you rethink your choices. Give you a chance to apologize properly. But you never did.”

“Because I’m not sorry,” Daniel retorted.

“Not yet,” Drake snarled. “Maybe I’ve been too nice to you. If you wanted me to put you in your place so badly, you just had to-”

“Hey!”

Daniel twisted his head at the new voice, his heart in his throat. Buck was standing right there, looking angrier than Daniel had ever seen him. Drake turned a little to face him, which gave Daniel some breathing room.

“Get away from him!” Buck bellowed, stomping towards them in a cloud of fury.

“Don’t be like that,” Drake drawled, though he did back up more. Enough so that Buck could force himself between him and Daniel. “We were just having a chat.”

“I don’t care,” Buck snapped. “Fuck off.”

“That’s not very nice.”

“Buck,” Daniel tried, but his baby brother was too busy snarling at the police detective to pay him any mind. “Buck.”

“You’re done,” Buck said. “If you come anywhere near him again, I’ll-”

“You’ll what?” Drake sounded delighted. “Are you threatening a cop?”

“Buck, come on,” Daniel tried again, tugging at his brother’s arm. “Let’s just go.”

This time, at least, Buck listened. He kept close to Daniel’s side the entire way to the building entrance, turning around every other second to glare at Drake. The moment they were inside, he was pulling out his phone.

“Hey, Athena, yeah. How’s that EPO?... ‘Cause he was just here harassing Danny…”

Chapter 34

Buck acted like a guard dog the rest of the night. Despite leaving Drake behind in the building’s parking lot, he stuck close to Daniel’s side the entire way up to their apartment. When they got to their apartment, Buck practically shoved Daniel in ahead of him and then put the chain on the door. Something that became a problem later when Albert tried to get in and Buck seemed like he was about five seconds away from literally barking and snapping as he rushed to check who was at the door before Daniel had the chance.

Albert was very confused and very startled when he was finally let in, only to be greeted by Buck holding Daniel’s bat.

“Um.” The younger Han was wide-eyed. “Should… Should I go elsewhere?”

“No, you’re fine.” Daniel rolled his eyes and reached past Buck to snag Albert by the arm, pulling him into the apartment properly.

“Did anyone bother you in the parking lot?” Buck asked, poking his head through the doorway and turning his head to look down both ends of the hall.

“No?” Albert was getting even more confused. “Is something going on? Should we call the cops?”

“Everything’s fine,” Daniel told him. “Buck, let it go.”

His brother huffed but closed the door, locking it as thoroughly as he had before.

Buck did not let it up in the morning, either. He kept close to Daniel the entire way to the car, head twisting and turning as he looked about for any possible threat. It was the same routine when they got to the station, his baby brother only relaxing when they got inside. Which meant that Daniel was absolutely not going to tell him about the times that Drake ambushed him in the truck bay. Because while this whole thing was sweet, it was also going to get very old, very fast, and Buck would never give him any breathing room if he stopped viewing the station as a safe space.

Mendoza was in the locker room when they got in. He was sitting on one of the benches, lacing up his boots.

“Welcome back.” He raised his head to frown at Daniel. “We met your parents.”

“You met my-” Daniel turned to Buck. “They were here?”

“They were looking for you,” his brother answered, shoulders a little hunched as he buried his head in his locker.

Daniel withheld the groan, because Buck being stuck alone with Mom and Dad was not a good thing. He should have pulled on his big boy pants and come in, instead of hiding away from everyone, because his brother did not deserve to be stuck dealing with their parents on his own. There was the hope that being in public would mean they toned it down a bit, but he knew how unlikely that was if Mom was upset enough. She’d given Buck more than one dressing down in hospitals before, uncaring of how loud she got or how many people could hear.

“How bad were they?” Daniel asked.

“It was fine.” Buck didn’t bother making an attempt at meeting Daniel’s eyes as he said it. Daniel twisted around to look at Mendoza.

“We took care of ‘em,” was all the paramedic said, giving him a little nod. “Flowers and Nola and I.”

Daniel let out a breath as he nodded back. It was nice to know that he could trust his baby brother with their coworkers, that he could trust them to watch his back when he wasn’t there for more than just the risks of the job. Then again, it wasn’t all that surprising: they’d all been there and watched as Buck was pinned beneath the ladder truck on live television, and they’d all started treating him like the shift’s collective younger brother when he transferred.

“So where were ya last shift?” Mendoza asked. “You don’t normally take off like that.”

“Wasn’t feeling well,” was all Daniel said. He saw Mendoza glance at Buck, as if he might provide more of an answer, but Buck was too busy changing and didn’t notice.

“Well, heads up. Stoppard was saying you owe him, now.”

“Owe him? What the hell, I’ve covered for him twice since he started!”

“Hey, don’t shoot the messenger,” Mendoza said, raising his hands. “I’m just telling you what he was saying.”

“What an asshole.”

The shift was, at least, not very busy. They went on two calls by the afternoon, neither of them very stressful. Buck spent half the time distracted, head twisting around every few moments like he was expecting Drake to just suddenly appear. Not that Daniel knew what Buck was expecting to do if that happened, beyond causing a scene and/or getting himself arrested.

Another cop did show up shortly after they came back from the second call. Athena walked into the truck bay in her uniform while Daniel was doing a once-over of the engine, acting every bit like she belonged there and paying no mind to the odd looks from the others. Buck, having never wandered very far from Daniel the entire day, appeared at his side just as she reached him.

“So?” his younger brother, ever impatient, blurted out.

Daniel rolled his eyes. He seriously did not know what Buck was expecting. No, that was a lie, he did know. He was expecting cops investigating cops to actually care and do something. Which was sweet and adorable, but definitely not going to-

“The judge approved the EPO,” Athena said, and then paused for Buck’s cheer.

Daniel blinked.

“A judge… What?”

“Approved the EPO.” The sergeant might’ve sounded a bit smug, but Daniel was too caught on the words she was saying to pay attention to her tone. “Another officer is informing Mr. Drake now.”

“That’s great news,” Buck said. He threw an arm around Daniel’s shoulders and jostled him a little.

“How?” Daniel blurted out. “Why?”

“I knew the judge,” Athena said. “I told him the two of you had a relationship, you ended it, and now he’s harassing you. Which isn’t technically a lie.”

“A relationship?” He swallowed back the hysterical laughter. “Athena, I was a-”

“The charges were dropped by the El Paso DA’s office,” she reminded him, keeping her words hushed. “There’s no evidence except his word, and he is harassing his ex.”

“So what happens now?” Buck asked her while Daniel was left reeling. There was no way it was this easy. Nothing was this easy.

“The protection order is only for a week.” Athena was answering Buck’s question, but she was speaking to Daniel. “You’ll have to file for a restraining order, but it isn’t difficult. I’ll get the forms and bring them to the apartment for you.”

“But.” Daniel’s tongue felt heavy. “He’s a cop.”

“He’s a detective, which means there’ll be few reasons for him showing up on scenes with you at all,” Athena said. The way she wasn’t even addressing the point he was trying for had to be intentional. “If he does show up, it won’t be because dispatch sent him.”

“And if he shows up here?” Buck asked, and Daniel twisted his head to look at him so fast he almost gave himself whiplash. Surely he didn’t know that Drake had shown up here, there was no way. “The station’s public, isn’t it? People come here for help, sometimes.”

“It’s your brother’s place of employment, so coming here violates the EPO.” Athena was staring at Daniel, a singular eyebrow raised. She hadn’t missed his reaction. “Again, he’s a detective. There’s little reason for him to be coming here short of an emergency. If there’s a case involving the One Thirty-three or the One Eighteen, like the bank heist, they’ll hand it to another detective.”

“The One Eighteen?”

“He was threatening Eddie’s son,” she said with a shrug. “That got covered, too.”

“Thank you, Athena.”

“Of course.” She smiled at Buck and then Daniel. “Like I said, I’ll swing by with the forms you’ll need to fill out.”

“Uh, yeah. Alright.” Daniel nodded dumbly as he and Buck watched the sergeant leave. He stood there for a moment, before turning to Buck and saying, “I’m going to, um. Get something to drink. Or something.”

Maybe have a lie down, he thought, as he left Buck there before his brother could give a response. A lie down sounded good.

The fire stood out against the night sky, which was its usual black urban void with the occasional pin prick of light. The 133 had been the first to show up on the scene, with the 141 arriving shortly after, for a fire at an industrial complex. Specifically, a perfume factory that was converted into a hand sanitizer factory when the pandemic struck. Accelerants abounded, but they had no idea where they were stored because the factory hadn’t filed any certificates after the conversion. The sprinkler system failed, which they were trying to get them operational again without much success so far, and there were factory workers unaccounted for.

“This is a mess,” Buck said to no one in particular, the front of his turnouts wet from the spray of the hoses.

“So you keep saying.” Danny gave him a gentle shove forward to where Mehta waited in his white Incident Command helmet.

“Buckleys!” their captain called when they got close enough. “This entire thing is-”

“A mess,” Buck repeated. Danny rolled his eyes and bumped their shoulders together.

“I was gonna say death trap,” Mehta said. “I’m sending the two of you in with some from the One Eighteen, through alpha side, while another team goes in through charlie. There’s twelve workers still unaccounted for. You get them, you get out.”

“Got it, Cap,” they chorused.

They jogged for the engine to tug on their SCBA gear, Buck grabbing an ax as well, and then he and Danny hauled a hose to the doors they were going in through. Buck tried not to be too obviously disappointed when it was Hen and Chimney and Austin there, the latter cutting through the lock with a buzzsaw, and not Eddie. Eddie was, Buck supposed, part of the other team on the other side of the building.

Austin handed off the saw and then opened the doors. Flames immediately burst out and he staggered back a bit.

“Knock it down, boys!” Chimney shouted, voice muffled by his oxygen mask. Danny and Buck moved forward, spraying the flames with the hose. Soon, there was nothing except steam and smoke, and Danny switched it off.

Listening to Hen’s cry of “to the left!”, Buck went that way. There was more fire in that direction - there was fire everywhere - but it was the containers that had him freezing in his boots. Barrels with warning labels plastered all over their sides that read things like “Explosive!” and “Caution! Flammable!” and other things that could be simply translated thusly: This + Fire = Bad. Very, very bad.

There were shelves full of containers of hand sanitizer, too. Each of them was a grenade waiting to be lit, and the flames were inching ever closer.

“IC, this is Buck,” he radioed, eyes fixed on the bombs in front of him.  “I’ve got level four flammables inside the west side entry. Looks like about ten pressurized drums.”

“Copy that,” Mehta responded. “Sprinkler systems are still down, so I’m sending in foam.”

“Alright, guys, let me know the level of involvement up ahead,” Hen said, motioning as she spoke. “The victims are toward that side of the building.”

Buck and Chimney jogged forward, splitting when the path was disrupted by shelves and fire. Buck made a circuit, and he was soon back with the others.

“I wouldn’t say it was all clear,” Buck reported. “But it’s definitely clear enough for us to keep on moving.”

“This way is no good,” Chimney told them, returning from his own short scouting mission.

“Let’s keep going your way then, Buck,” Hen said. 

She motioned to the others, and the group marched forward on the path that Buck took. There was a door, not far from the way they got in. It looked like it might’ve led into an office. What caught Buck’s attention, however, was the bottom of it.

“Hey, wait, here!” he called out, waving for everyone’s attention. “Someone put towels under the door to keep the smoke out!”

There was a window, shatterproof glass lined through with little ribbons of metal. It was dark on the other side, but Buck could make out moving shapes. The door was stuck, but his ax took care of that easily. When he got it opened, he stepped out of the way for the others to rush inside.

“IC, Captain Nash here,” came through the radio. Buck listened as he did a mental headcount of the people they’d found. “Be advised we have located seven victims, but we’ve had some accelerants ignite up here. We are separated from two of our team, sending them back out.”

“You guys hear that?” Buck asked the others. “They need help.”

“On the other side of the factory!” Danny pointed out.

“They lost two guys, we’ve got plenty here,” Buck argued. “I should go.”

If there was something he’d learned from this mess with Drake and Danny, it was that he hadn’t been a very good brother. And while maybe he hadn’t been made to be a good brother, he had been made with the intent of making Danny better. Yet it seemed he’d just made things worse for him. Buck didn’t know how to make up for that, but there were other things he could do in the meanwhile.

Like be a good firefighter, for one.

“He’s not wrong,” Hen said. “And I don’t say that often.”

“This is a death trap,” Danny snapped, and then shook his head when Buck looked at him pleadingly. “Fine. Fine! But be careful. I’ll hunt you down and drag you out myself if I have to.”

Buck nodded and jogged off towards the eastern side of the structure, the charlie side, where Bobby and his group entered. It wasn’t a quick or straightforward journey, the way blocked by fire and more of those barrels just waiting to explode. More than once he had to backtrack and go a different route, and his sense of direction was starting to become unreliable. Mostly, he was following the wall and trusting it to take him the way he needed to go.

He was just resorting to climbing up a ladder up onto a gantry when the entire building shook with an explosion. It rocked Buck, nearly throwing him off, and his radio burst into life almost instantly.

“IC, be advised.” That wasn’t a voice he knew. Must have been someone from the 141, maybe, or another station that had joined them. “That last explosion took out most of the supports in here. Structural integrity is not good.”

Aw, shit.

“All teams, all teams, be advised. We are evacuating the structure.” Mehta’s voice cut through as Buck used the gantry to get over a hotspot. “Repeat, full evacuation is in effect.”

“IC, this is Buck,” he radioed back. “One team found seven victims, others got four. Means there’s still someone in here.”

“We’re aware, Buck, but it’s too unstable.”

“We’re just gonna leave someone behind?” What the hell? No, Buck couldn’t just abandon someone in this. Not if there was a chance he could get them out.

“It’s too dangerous to continue,” Mehta replied. “You need to pull out, now.”

“Copy that, on the move,” Buck answered. There was a door right there, marked as the exit. And he could go that way, or…

He turned his back on it and ran in the other direction, towards where the last person was supposed to be. And then he cringed at the next voice on the radio.

“Evan Christopher Buckley.” Oh, Danny did not sound happy.

“I’m moving, I’m moving!”

This was fine. It was going to be fine. Buck had every intention of getting out, he was just making a quick stop first. Find the worker, grab him, and get out. Technically it wasn’t lying or ignoring orders- Okay, so he had to accept that he couldn’t loophole his way out of that last one, because he very much was ignoring orders, but he definitely wasn’t lying.

He just said he was on the move. It wasn’t entirely his fault if they interpreted that as him moving for the exit.

(Maybe he’d get lucky and one of these barrels would take him out before he had to face his very pissed off brother.)

The rhythmic banging of metal on metal made Buck feel very good about his life choices at that moment. Especially when, after he called out, the banging got louder and picked up pace. It had to be the last worker, signalling for help. He followed the sound, on path that was not as direct as he would like, shouting to them all the way.

Buck found the last worker crouched behind some machinery. He rushed for him.

“Are you hurt?” he asked.

“I am lost,” was the worker’s answer. “Too much smoke.”

“That’s okay, we’re gonna get out of here. Can you breathe?”

“This is helping.” The worker gestured at the N95 mask he was wearing. “But the fire is not.”

“Then let’s make it quick, c’mon.”

Buck helped the man to his feet, urging him to stay low as he guided them towards the exit. Or, he tried to get them to the exit. They turned a corner, and fire flared. A quick backtrack and another corner led to the same result.

Back in El Paso, Buck would hang out at Danny’s station a lot on weekends or after school or on breaks. Usually, when he wasn’t babysitting for Alma or running around with Eddie or wasn’t working somewhere for spending money, he’d go bother his brother at work. The guys there didn’t mind too terribly much.

There was one firefighter Danny worked with, a man named Gabe, who would regale Buck with stories about calls he’d been on while Danny did his chores. The thing that always stuck out to Buck was how Gabe would talk about fire like it was this living, breathing, hungry beast. The way he spoke, it was almost like the fire in his stories was an animal stalking its prey.

That was how Buck felt in that moment, a deer being herded by a pack of wolves. But he wasn’t going to just give up, not here, not now. There were other ways out, there had to be.

“I think I see an exterior wall,” Buck said, pointing. The problem was, though, that the way forward was blocked by fire here, too.

“Let us hope it is equipped with a door.”

Buck seconded that.

“What’s your name?” he asked the worker.

“Saleh.”

“Alright, Saleh, I think we’re gonna have to walk across this gantry.” There was one right above the fire. The smoke was thick up there, and the heat would be almost unbearable, but it was both their best and perhaps only way out of this trap that Buck had led them into. “You think you can make it?”

“I would like nothing more than to make it,” Saleh said. Buck decided he liked this guy.

They climbed up, Buck urging Saleh ahead of him. For the briefest of moments, it seemed like it would be fine, that they would make it. And then, below them, a barrel ignited, combusted, exploded. It took out one of the supports for the gantry and sent them both tumbling. Buck’s helmeted head slammed into something metallic that clanged with the impact.

He wasn’t awake when he hit the ground.

Chapter 35

Buck came to on concrete with a rampaging headache. For a moment, before he blinked open his eyes, he had the absurd thought that he was back with Connor and them. The headache felt the same as the ones he would get when the ragers they threw raged a little bit too hard. It wouldn’t be the first time he’d woken up in odd places after a night of fun, and at least this time he wasn’t naked.

Except, as he took in his hellish surroundings, the present stampeded into him. He scrambled up, ignoring the way the world tilted for a moment, and looked for-

“Saleh!”

The man wasn’t far from Buck. He was laying on his back, but he was awake and aware.

“Thank you for trying to save me, but it appears this vat had a different plant.” The vat in question being the one that was currently pinning Saleh to the ground by his legs. Buck wondered if it was the one he hit with his head on the way down. “It is also very heavy.”

It was. Buck’s first instinct was to try and lift it up, at least enough for Saleh to pull himself clear and to safety. Except that he couldn’t get it to budge, not even a little. He remembered being stuck under the ladder truck, how agonizing it was to feel it shifting on top of his leg, but Saleh was just laying there.

An attempt to use his ax, tucked into his belt, as a lever didn’t give any better results. He gave up with a quiet curse, panting from exertion, and took in their surroundings. It was looking very grim.

“I’m gonna need you to try and stay calm, okay?” Buck told Saleh, kneeling down beside him. Really, the words were more for himself. “I’m gonna get this thing off you, and I’m gonna get you out of here.”

He clung to the promise as he made it. Because the alternative, where only one of them got out - or worse, neither of them - was not a reality he was willing to entertain.

“You will need to hurry,” Saleh told him. His gaze was fixed on something beyond Buck. When he turned, he realized that he’d underestimated the grimness of their situation.

There was a pool of sanitizer on the floor. A leak from somewhere, maybe one of the toppled vats or it could be that one of the barrels burst or- Ah, there, a bunch of canisters had fallen and were spilling out. As it spread across the space, so too did the fire. It was getting far too close to the both of them for Buck’s liking.

And the sprinklers still weren’t on.

It was with great relief that Eddie stepped out of the inferno that was once a factory, allowing the 141 to shepherd the workers they rescued to the ambulances. Up ahead, he spotted 118 helmets - Hen and Chimney and Austin - along with a singular 133. He would never admit aloud to being disappointed when he saw Buckley on the turnout coat only for it to be Danny who turned around, oxygen mask in his hand.

The man’s eyes flickered between them, then past them. His face drew into a scowl.

“Where’s Buck?” he demanded.

“What do you mean?” Bobby asked in return.

“I thought he’d be with you,” Eddie added.

“He split off when you lost two of your guys.” Hen explained. 

Eddie felt his heart lurch. They were on opposite sides of the building, and if he was understanding the implication there, then Buck had tried crossing the hellish blaze inside to reach them. He hadn’t made it, so anything could’ve-

“IC, Cap, this is Buck.”

The sound of Buck’s voice over the radio had them all turning to the command tent. As Mehta grabbed his radio mic, looking particularly perturbed, they rushed over to listen in.

“Buck, did you ignore my direct order to evacuate?” the 133’s captain asked.

“He hasn’t done that to you before?” Bobby asked, humor lacing his voice.

Danny glared at him for the comment, not that the fire captain seemed to notice. Or maybe he did and was just choosing to ignore it.

“I got the last victim, but this sanitizer has ignited all around me,” Buck said. Danny took on the wide-eyed, frantic expression that Eddie recognized from the waiting room of the hospital after the ladder truck, when Danny paced endlessly and snapped at everyone who fell into his line of sight. It was the beginning of the look Danny wore when he shoved Bobby out of his way to get to his brother when Buck had the embolism. “I wanna say I’m near the northeast corner, Delta wall, but I’m not sure. I could use some sprinkler action. Th- They online yet?”

Eddie saw Danny flinch slightly at how Buck’s voice broke slightly with the question.

“Negative, but hang tight. We’re gonna get you both out,” Mehta said, and then switched channels on his radio. “RIC team, RIC team, deploy. Delta entrance, northeast corner. Repeat, Delta entrance, northeast corner.”

“We’re coming, squirt,” Danny said into his radio. He’d already pulled his oxygen mask back on and was now striding back to the fire. Mehta made an aborted motion, as if he was going to try and pull him back, and then just huffed in exasperation.

Eddie glanced at Bobby and the others, and then he hurried to do the same.

“Copy you. Not going anywhere.”

“I am going to kill him,” Danny was saying. Not to anyone in particular, Eddie thought. “I am going to drag him out by his ear and then I am going to kill him.”

It was probably a good thing that Danny’s radio wasn’t live at that moment. Eddie didn’t think Buck would be willing to be rescued if he heard how angry his brother was. The explosion that sent fire blasting out of the windows and had them all ducking on instinct seemed to only incense Danny further.

It had not been much of an exaggeration to think of all the containers of hand sanitizer as bombs waiting to go off. Buck wasn’t certain where that explosion had originated from, but it had sent fire billowing forth throughout the interior. He’d covered Saleh with his body as best he could, and felt the heat of it on every bit of exposed skin. But thankfully, the rules of physics were on their side here, and all of that had gone up and over them.

“Are you okay?” Buck asked as he got to his feet.

“That is a relative term,” Saleh answered, sounding weaker by the moment. His breath was starting to be laboured, probably from the smoke and the heat. The N95 masks could only do so much here. “But I am alright.”

Saleh was right about it being relative at the moment. He was still pinned by the vat, and the fire was crawling ever closer to them. The latter was the most pressing matter, and something he should be able to take care of, at least long enough to give them some breathing room. If he could find the right tool for the job.

“What are you looking for?” Saleh asked him.

“I was a fire marshall once,” Buck explained. He still remembered all the various fire codes he’d needed to know, even though he hadn’t done the job for very long. “This is a factory. They’re required to have fire extinguishers three feet off the ground.”

Then again, he was getting the feeling that this place wasn’t particularly keen on following safety regulations. Oh! Right there, a few feet away and on the other side of some toppled machinery, was a fire extinguisher laying on the ground. It must have gotten knocked loose by one of the explosions.

“Okay, Saleh, I see- Saleh?”

The man was gasping now and Buck rushed back to his side, taking off his helmet so he could yank off his oxygen mask. There just wasn’t enough clean oxygen around them now for Saleh to breathe, and who knew how bad his lungs were at this point. The man looked up at him with bleary eyes as Buck switched out their masks, tossing the N95 aside and placing his oxygen mask over Saleh’s face.

“Just breathe,” Buck instructed. “In and out.”

“But how will you breathe?”

“I’m gonna hold it.”

“For how long?”

“As long as I can,” Buck answered, doing his best to keep up the cheer. It was up to him, after all. It was all up to him to get the both of them out of here.

It was a simple matter to slide over the machinery, grab the extinguisher, and then hurry back. The extinguisher wasn’t a miracle tool, but it smothered the fire that had gotten far too close for comfort. That much and no more, before it was empty and useless. Buck dropped it to the ground with a clang of metal on concrete, and then dropped to his knees beside Saleh to check on him.

The man was wearing thin, blinking up at him and not really reacting to Buck’s attempts to rouse him. The fall, perhaps, or the vat’s weight, or the heat, or too much time without clean oxygen. It didn’t matter what, because the result was the same: they were running out of time for the both of them to get out of this mess.
